articles.title: Everton drop Jack Grealish from Carabao Cup tie over ‘breach of club discipline’
articles.summary: England player left out of squad to face Newcastle. Moyes confirms he ‘supports’ the club decision. Jack Grealish was dropped from Everton’s Carabao Cup win over Newcastle following a breach of club discipline.
body: Everton took the unusual step of announcing that Grealish’s omission from the fourth-round tie was for disciplinary reasons on social media, after listing David Moyes’s team for the fourth-round tie at Hill Dickinson Stadium. The club posted on X: “Jarrad Branthwaite remains sidelined for a second successive game due to concussion protocols, while Jack Grealish is unavailable for selection due to a breach of club discipline.”
It is understood the 31-year-old missed training on Monday without permission and the decision to drop him was taken by Moyes in conjunction with the Everton chief executive Angus Kinnear.
Speaking after Everton’s 3-1 win, Moyes said: “I’m not going to give any details. It was a club decision and I support it. I don’t want to speak too much about it.”

Grealish returned to training at Everton’s Finch Farm complex after Monday’s absence but is expected to be fined for his unauthorised absence earlier in the week. The playmaker had missed Everton’s defeat at Arsenal on Saturday due to illness.

articles.title: George Russell determined not to let disappointing F1 season define career
articles.summary: 28-year-old still believes he will win world title one day. Kimi Antonelli misses media duties with ‘viral illness’ George Russell has insisted he will not let his difficult Formula One season define his career and believes he still has plenty of years left to come back and win the world…
body: Russell has been out-driven by his 20-year-old Mercedes teammate Kimi Antonelli in what has been a bruising season for the British driver. Antonelli is set to win the title and become F1’s youngest world champion at this weekend’s Mexican Grand Prix if he finishes in ninth place or above.

He has taken nine wins thus far to Russell’s three, with the British driver struggling for consistency in adapting to the demands of the energy management required by the new cars which, alongside the tyres in use this year, does not suit the 28-year-old’s driving style.

Russell has delivered some impeccable weekends, including commanding performances in Austria and Baku to victory but more often than not has been left baffled as to why he cannot make the car work to the same effect as Antonelli, a process which he conceded had been hard to deal with.

“I’ve probably learned more about myself this year than I would have liked to in all honesty,” he said at the Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez. “You know, the highs and lows you go through in sport are immense and that’s because we all care so much for what we’re doing.

articles.title: Everton ease past Newcastle to set up Fleetwood trip after Grealish is dropped
articles.summary: A big night for Everton featured a big call from David Moyes and demanded a big performance from his players. With the exception of Jack Grealish, they did not let him down.
body: Newcastle dominated spells of the fourth round tie and the stats – registering 28 shots to Everton’s 11, although only nine visiting attempts were on target – but individual defensive errors and an ineffective attack proved a ruinous combination. Matthias Jaissle denied his team are a soft touch, despite persuasive evidence to the contrary, yet called Newcastle “naive” and the defeat, in front of almost 8,000 of their fans, “shocking”. Prime minister Andy Burnham was among the many Evertonians in attendance grateful for Newcastle’s generosity.

James Garner, with his first goal of the season, Hayden Hackney, with his first goal for the club, and Thierno Barry were on target to take Everton into the last eight of a competition they have never won. Jordan Pickford was in commanding form against his old adversaries while Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall ran the show from midfield. But it was the absent Grealish who dominated the buildup after Everton announced he had been dropped for disciplinary reasons.

articles.title: PSG claim late point after Shaw penalty to hit Manchester City’s WCL top-four hopes
articles.summary: Manchester City’s hopes of securing a top-four spot in the Women’s Champions League are looking increasingly slim after a third successive draw dragged out their wait for a first European victory of the season, by virtue of Paris Saint-Germain’s late leveller at a disappointed Joie Stadium.
body: You cannot miss half a dozen strong chances at Women’s Champions League level and expect to get away with it. That is the harsh lesson Manchester City learnt on Thursday against Paris Saint-Germain, who extended the English champions’s wait for their first win in Europe this season by striking late to secure a point at a disappointed Joie Stadium.

City’s third draw from three Champions League games so far this season really ought to have been a victory. Instead, their hopes of a top-four spot and with it automatic qualification for the quarter-finals are looking increasingly slim.

They thought they had won the game through Khadija ‘Bunny’ Shaw’s 85th-minute penalty, but conceding sparked PSG into life and they snatched a point with a scrappy equaliser three minutes later as their substitute Tara Elimbi Gilbert found the net from close range.

How, therefore, should we look upon City’s season? Are they the team that is unbeaten in all competitions? Or the team without a win in Europe? Both ring true, and although they are still likely to progress to the knockout stages, they will have been hugely frustrated with their profligacy.

articles.title: Ireland's Furlong cleared of groin grab by disciplinary committee
articles.summary: Ireland's Tadhg Furlong is cleared by a disciplinary committee of grabbing Gavin Coombes in the groin during Leinster's United Rugby Championship win over Munster.
body: Munster back row Coombes raised the allegation with match referee Andrew Brace in the first half of Leinster's 24-18 win at Aviva Stadium, but television match official (TMO) Colin Stanley could not find conclusive video evidence.

However, three-time British and Irish Lions tourist Furlong was subsequently cited over an act of foul play under Law 9.27, which says "a player must not do anything that is against the spirit of good sportsmanship including but not limited to grabbing, twisting or squeezing the genitals".

The disciplinary panel, comprised of Simon Thomas (Wales), Attie Heyns (South Africa) and Pamela Woodman (Scotland) met on Thursday and "unanimously concluded the citing complaint against the player should be dismissed, on the basis that he did not commit an act of foul play contrary to Law 9.27".
While they dismissed the complaint, the disciplinary committee concluded Coombes had given "an honest account of his recollection of events surrounding the incident".

articles.title: Russell: 2026 F1 season won't break me
articles.summary: George Russell insists this year's Formula 1 season "won't break me" as Kimi Antonelli is set to become world champion this weekend in Mexico.
body: A top nine finish for Antonelli, or Russell or Lewis Hamilton failing to win Sunday's Mexico City Grand Prix, would secure the title for the Italian, who would be the youngest champion in F1 history at 20 years old.
Russell came into 2026 as favourite after dominating Antonelli last year but has won just three races to his team-mate's nine, regularly being outperformed throughout the season.

"I've probably learned more about myself this year than I would have liked to in all honesty. The highs and lows you go through in sport are immense. That's because we all care so much for what we're doing," said Russell.
"I remind myself I'm 28 years old. I see Lewis still competing extremely well at 41 and Fernando at 44. Lewis won the majority of his titles in his 30s.

articles.title: 'Lack of talent' - Alonso doubles down on Albon criticism
articles.summary: Aston Martin's Fernando Alonso has doubled down on his criticism of "low level" Formula 1 drivers who have a "lack of talent" following his collision with Williams' Alex Albon in Austin.
body: Albon tried to overtake Alonso for 12th place into the Turn 11 hairpin on the opening lap of the United States Grand Prix, but went into the side of the Aston Martin driver, damaging both cars.
Neither driver received a penalty and both were able to continue with Alonso finishing 16th and Albon in 17th in Austin.

Post-race, Alonso stated the quality of the drivers in the bottom third of F1's grid is "very low" and he had not changed his stance in Thursday's media day ahead of this weekend's Mexico City Grand Prix.
"I think it's simply a very low level of driving and lack of talent," he told Sky Sports F1.

Mercedes also have an opportunity to wrap up the Constructors' Championship but would need to outscore Ferrari by 39 points.
Lando Norris won last year's Mexico City Grand Prix but McLaren have faded in form over the last month, with Red Bull and Ferrari proving to be Mercedes' biggest challengers.
Max Verstappen has won at the Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez a record five times but all eyes will be on Antonelli and whether he can win the title in style.

articles.title: 📋 Grêmio line up to escape bottom four; Athletico target top three
articles.summary: This Thursday (29), Grêmio and Athletico-PR face off at the Arena in Porto Alegre at 9:30 p.m. (Brasília time), in the final match of Matchday 33 of the 2026 Brasileirão.
body: Grêmio sit in the first relegation spot (17th place) with just 34 points and are chasing a second straight win to push archrivals Inter (35 points) into the relegation zone.
Athletico-PR, meanwhile, sit fourth with 54 points despite going two matches without a win.

Cruzeiro and Fluminense have the same number of points, but the Minas Gerais side are one place above thanks to more wins (16 to 15), while the Rio de Janeiro side are one place below on goal difference (+12 to +10).

Compared with their last match (a 1-1 draw with Vitória), coach Odair Hellmann has brought Arthur Dias, Léo Derik and Portilla into Athletico-PR's lineup in place of Bruno, Gilberto and Jadson, respectively.

articles.title: Everton boss Moyes backs 'club decision' to drop Grealish for Newcastle tie
articles.summary: David Moyes pointedly praised Everton's "really good values" after Jack Grealish was dropped for breaching club discipline prior to Thursday's 3-1 win over Newcastle in the League Cup.
body: Grealish reportedly skipped training ahead of the fourth round tie and was left out of the Everton squad at the Hill Dickinson Stadium.
The on-loan Manchester City winger had missed Everton's defeat at Arsenal in the Premier League on Saturday due to illness.
Everton boss Moyes refused to give further details on Grealish's absence against Newcastle, but backed the move to leave him out.
"It was a club decision. I support the decision. It's something I don't really want to speak too much about," he said.
